examples/factorial:
{"stand":{"box":[null,{"scale":["5","5"]},"bird"]},"bench":[{"nest":["120"]},{"text":"FACTORIAL

Give the team [N, a bird].

The first robot builds the
rest: a scale with 1 in one
pan and N in the other, and
"so far" joined on in front.

Then two robots take turns
by reading the scale --
leaning means keep going,
level means answer."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Give the two-hole box to the
Factorial robot.

Watch the scale come level
as the count climbs to N.

5! = 120 arrives on the
nest marked "N factorial".

Nothing counts rounds: the
scale is the only test."}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/swap:
{"stand":{"scale":["3","7"]},"bench":[{"scale":["2","9"]},{"text":"SWAP

A scale is a balance: put
a number in each pan and
it leans towards the
heavier one.

The robot's thought is "a
scale leaning left" -- the
numbers themselves are not
in the thought at all, only
which way it leans."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Give the leaning scale to
the Swap robot. It puts the
two numbers the other way
round, the scale leans the
other way, and the robot
stops -- because its thought
no longer matches.

Give it the other scale and
nothing happens: that one is
already in order."}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/infinity/activity1-even-numbers:
{"stand":null,"bench":[{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"nest":["16","14","12","10","8","6","4","2"]},{"nest":["7","5","3","1"]},{"nest":["8","6","4","2"]},{"text":"ACTIVITY 1
The even numbers, two ways

Add 1 makes 1, 2, 3, ... for
ever. Both rooms are fed from
that one sequence.

Doubler doubles each: the
evens, out of EVERY natural.

Split deals them out left,
right, left: A gets the odds
and B the evens -- out of
every OTHER natural.

Watch B and doubled fill at
the same rate. Same sequence,
two ways. One of them looks
as if it should be half the
size of the other."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Set Rounds to 12 and pull the
lever on the Add 1 room.

That is all. Every robot is
already in place; the three
rooms work at the same time,
each waking as the first
number reaches it.

Watch B and doubled fill at
the same rate.

Then ask: is there an even
number on B that is not on
doubled? Will there ever be?"}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/infinity/activity2-all-integers:
{"stand":null,"bench":[{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"nest":["8","-7","7","-6","6","-5","5","-4","4","-3","3","-2","2","-1","1"]},{"text":"ACTIVITY 2
Combining sequences, part 1

Add 1 makes 1, 2, 3, ... and
feeds both rooms at once.

Negator turns each into its
negative. Merge takes one from
each nest in turn and hands
the result out.

Merge keeps no count. It gives
away what is on the first nest
and then swaps the two nests
over -- so next round it reads
the other. The swap IS the
alternation.

Neither side can run ahead, so
every integer arrives after a
finite wait. Countable."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Set Rounds to 12 and pull the
lever on the Add 1 room.

All three rooms run together.

Merge lags one behind Negator:
it will not hand out a positive
until the matching negative has
arrived. That is it being fair.

Then ask: is there an integer
that never reaches the last
nest, however long it runs?"}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/infinity/activity4-all-fraction:
{"stand":null,"bench":[{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"nest":[{"box":["3","4"]},{"box":["2","4"]},{"box":["1","4"]},{"box":["2","3"]},{"box":["1","3"]},{"box":["1","2"]}]},{"nest":["1/2"]},{"text":"ACTIVITY 4
All fractions between 0 and 1

You cannot list the fractions
in order of size: between any
two there is another, so there
is no first step to take.

So walk them by DENOMINATOR:

  1/2 | 1/3 2/3 | 1/4 2/4 3/4
  | 1/5 2/5 3/5 4/5 | ...

Each group is finite, so the
walk reaches every fraction
after finitely many steps.

The branch is the SCALE. While
it tips towards the bottom
number, Next Numerator runs.
When it BALANCES, that robot
no longer matches and Next
Denominator takes the turn."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Set Rounds to 20 and pull the
lever on the All Fractions
room.

The scale pans are holes: walk
in through the door and watch
the numbers in them climb.

Then ask: does 2/4 appear? And
1/2 as well? They are the same
number written twice -- which
is what the No Copies robot in
the original set exists to fix.

Does every proper fraction turn
up eventually? Which step
reaches 7/8?"}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/infinity/activity6-all-rational:
{"stand":null,"bench":[{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"nest":["2","1/2"]},{"text":"ACTIVITY 6
All the positive rationals

Nothing new is built here. The
rooms hold, in order:

  All Fractions   (activity 4)
  Box to Number   (activity 4)
  Divides 1       (activity 5)
  Merge           (activity 2)

Below-1 goes one way and is
turned over to make above-1;
Merge then takes one from each
in strict alternation.

What comes out is a QUEUE of
all the positive rationals.

Between any two rationals lie
infinitely many more. Not one
of them has a next. And still
they can be stood in a line
and counted off."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Set Rounds to 24 and pull the
lever on the All Fractions
room.

Five rooms wake in turn as the
first fraction reaches them.

Merge lags: it will not hand
out a fraction until the
matching reciprocal has
arrived. That is fairness, and
fairness is what makes the
count work.

Does 1 itself ever appear? Does
any number appear twice? What
would you have to add to stop
that -- and does it matter to
the argument?"}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/live-account:
{"stand":null,"bench":["150",{"nest":["150","140","130","120","110"]},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"text":"THE ACCOUNT, ON A PANEL

The balance is a LIVE
number. The old teller
robot is gone: depositing
is a +badge to its bird,
reading is [query | bird],
watching is [listen | bird].

Two rooms deposit at once.
Each badge is applied whole
-- no interleaving can tear
a deposit -- so 100, plus
five 10s, plus four 25s, is
250 however the rounds
happen to land."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Pull both levers.

Tenner banks +10 while its
scale tips: five times.
Quarter banks +25 four
times. Each stops when its
beam comes level.

The statement nest keeps
the history, newest
underneath.

A level beam is a robot
STOPPED -- its lever will
say so. To bank again, step
in through the door and set
the left pan back to 1."}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
examples/gauge:
{"stand":null,"bench":["5","5",{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"room":{"has":true,"dirty":false}},{"text":"THE GAUGE

A and B are live numbers.

Sync dozes on A's events;
each change flies to B
wearing a set badge. Control
does the same the other way.

Change EITHER -- drop a
number on it, or send its
bird a badge -- and the
other follows.

The echo rule is why this
ring does not ring forever:
a set that changes nothing
is swallowed, so the circle
stops after one lap."},{"text":"TO RUN IT

Pull both levers up.

Drop a +3 on A. Watch B
follow. Drop a ×2 on B.
Watch A follow.

The events nests keep the
history: every value each
number has passed through,
newest underneath."}],"copyIn":null,"copyOut":null}
